title: Want to Check Out Yet Another LLM RPG?
author: Aromatic-Low-4578
selftext:
I built [https://nervejack.gg](https://nervejack.gg) and would love your feedback. I've been working on this on and off for almost a year at this point.  It seems like such an obvious use case for an LLM but is one of those problems that seems much simpler than it is. I spent quite a while trying to figure out how to do this with local LLMs, then trying to figure out how to distribute it in a way that gamers would be able to easily install.  The overall progression was: CLI app with local model -> CLI app with a finetuned local model -> Web app using .onnx models -> Godot app

I finally just wanted to see if the concept worked, so I bit the bullet and made it using cloud providers. I think it's in a pretty good place and I have genuinely interesting, funny and poignant moments in it but I'd love any input you all have. Also happy to discuss all the stuff that didn't work. Or worked but wasn't easily distributable.

comments.author: Am_Biyori
comments.body: Is there a goal that needs completing in order to finish a play though?

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body:
There is not. There are quests and the world will basically infinitely generate for you but there's no "finish".  
  
Something I'm actually struggling with at the moment is the idea of progression and what kind of progression should be in the game beyond completing quests (and not dying) open to ideas.  Not trying to copy a whole TTRPG system but I feel like there needs to be something.

comments.author: Hungry_River_9594
comments.body:
This is pretty damn good. I actually enjoy this over a conventional RPG, because instead of playing walking simulator to deliver a package, you just write "deliver package" and go through the grind of repeating it.

I like the sense of agency. It's enough to enjoy being able to do what I want and yet not like AI Dungeon where everyone's your bitch. The AI and the world does push back. There's a roll to seduce whatever. 

>!Tried to rob a guy for his noodles. Dude dropped a chip and told me he'd give me money (not noodles) if I picked it up. I picked it up. He told me I would be paid if I did another thing. I attacked him. He attacked did not kill me. I told him that I'd take the damn quest. He still had his knife out. I \*insisted\* on taking the quest. And yeah. Sets tension and plot twists unlike Claude !<  
Good experience, reminds me of Dwarf Fortress. Not yet good enough to wishlist, but maybe with some goals. There's no larger loop, it's just doing stuff in a world.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Thank you for checking it out! really appreciate the feedback.

comments.author: Exciting_Finance7499
comments.body: Damn I played all my free turns well done.  Not sure why you have it gated for the beta.  Just unlock everything right now to get feedback then lock once you have it all fleshed out. Was fun though well done.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body:
Thanks for checking it out! Turns are daily, you'll have 30 more tomorrow, but feel free to message me for a sub. 

I hear you about charging for a beta, the beta thing is mostly to give people a heads up that things will continue to change as I learn and tweak. I also don't want to run the risk of someone setting up an autoplaying script and draining my API credits.

comments.author: Audentes
comments.body:
That was way more fun than I expected. A few things for me...  
I tried to login after the 30 turns to save my play and it nuked my story I think. Not the end of the world, but you can get attached fast..  
It felt a bit easy to steer the story sometimes, maybe since I use AI  all the time? one character seemed to be more independent than the others and I enjoyed that better.  
Not sure how you're prompting the responses, but it was a bit repetitive. I don't have the logs anymore, but I noticed it started sentences the same way in the same response a few times.  

Overall you're onto something here. I could see a fun audiobook-style playthrough from the car too, if you had voice enabled and playback.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Thank you, I think I've just deployed a fix for that.  Really appreciate the feedback, it's definitely a fine line between keeping it challenging and keeping it approachable. I've begun to think it needs some sort of selectable difficulty level.

comments.author: turkey_sausage
comments.body:
This is nice. First ai gm I've tried in a while.
Status saved on account gen seems to work.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Thank you, really appreciate you mentioning that.

comments.author: MongooseEmpty4801
comments.body: I have never seen one of these that clicked for me. No real world building, no real player agency as nothing you do has any real effect on the world, so narrative to discover, etc.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: I never have either, that's why I built this. Have you tried it?  The world remembers it's state, the player is in complete control and yet bound to the rules of the world. At least that's the hope, if that's not your experience I'd love to hear any feedback you have.

replies.author: MongooseEmpty4801
replies.body: Remembering state is a far cry from world/lore/character depth.

comments.author: Real-Resident-3282
comments.body:
I did a couple runs worth of free tokens. It is a nice change from AI Dungeon and similar platforms to feel like there is a consistent world state and the items I pick up aren't going to be forgotten six messages from now.   
I was starting from scratch each time so I didn't really see the relationship score with any of the npcs I interacted with change over time but it is potentially a cool system. Also, you captured the Shadowrun / Snow Crash vibes real nicely.   
Overall, enjoyed it. Could maybe use a default plot / quest / nudge. These sort of sandboxes can feel a little aimless.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Thank you! Thanks for checking it out. I have recently added a quest progression system but am still in the process of testing it, it takes quite a few turns to develop.

comments.author: Satciel
comments.body:
I'm obsessed. I love it. My only issue is pretty typical I feel with Ai, sometimes characters transform into, well, something they weren't before. I had this character sprocket in my game whomst I loved and developed a good personality and relationship with. Now shes a little spider robot all of a sudden sadly. In head my head Canon she died because thats preferable to this. 

Just as well I love that the world actually pushes back. Starting out I used to type out some pretty amazing feats.

Which my character. Summarily, was unable to do of course. Quite humbling, and made me think about my choices.

As for permanent death, idk? Its AI so sometimes a mistyped ends in something ridiculous or near run ending.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Glad you're enjoying it! Did you just submit a feedback message about this?  One just came in that was quite similar. Planning to take a look ASAP, I try to address feedback within a day or two.

replies.author: Satciel
replies.body: Oh yes that was me, i realized I could submit feedback on the app. I think it might have something to do with me having drones, then naming them. So they end up being like a person, but also an inventory item? Just a wild guess.

replies.author: Satciel
replies.body: Thanks for immortalizing my drone Lucy in a way in the patch notes! Haha!

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Haha, no problem!  TBH your bug report was one of my favorites so far. Many are annoying things that I've been tweaking for a long time but this was a truly unique one that I never would have encountered in my own play-throughs. I love seeing people stretch the game like that.

Also, not sure if it's a thing or not, but I'd really like to find out if cyberware is a thing.

Cyberware exists but is getting an overhaul soon. It definitely needs to be fleshed out a bit more. 

Thanks for checking it out!

We'll keep returning for our little bite-sized adventures as an excuse to maintain the pace, and see where it goes. Voiceover narration does sound pretty cool..

comments.author: noapostrophe555
comments.body:
Long time TTRPG player. Checked the game out today to see if it was a viable alternative between game sessions. It was a very short experience with the 10 turn limit, but in that short time I was able to hack and break into a wrecked tram, get betrayed by and then kill my heist partner, and then get back home to check out the score from the heist. 

There's not a lot of feedback I can provide based off of my limited experience, but the ability to access things like notes on each encountered NPC is helpful - like campaign notes in a traditional TTRPG. One issue I noted was during the character creation process. There was flavor/detail text that would appear on the screen momentarily but disappeared before I could read it all.
